status: development evidence (dev Mac only); not qualification evidence. The owner's native Linux runner must re-observe every rule before any parity claim.

reference.build: Homebrew FFmpeg 9.0.2 (libavfilter 12.1.102, libswscale 10.1.102, libavutil 61.1.102); libswscale.10.1.102.dylib sha256 870934397a55bf3a229f1bd3bd66cfa70720b1e11fccad9f27bd98a56c2e20fa
reference.platform: macOS arm64, Apple M3 Pro (NEON code paths of that build)
reference.chain: buffer(colorspace, range from the decoded frame; graph nb_threads = 1) -> scale=1920:1080:force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease,pad=1920:1080:(ow-iw)/2:(oh-ih)/2,format=rgba -> buffersink (exactly harness/codecs/reference_decode.c)
reference.method: black box only: crafted planes through the public libavfilter API (harness/codecs/probe_rgba.c); no FFmpeg/libswscale source was opened or translated
reference.probe_equivalence: probe_rgba output on FFmpeg-decoded planes equals reference_decode raw output byte for byte (BA1_FT_C.264 prefix, 10 pictures; hevc-main10-1080p prefix, 15 complete pictures; the 16th differs only because the truncated stream decodes differently)

geometry.fit: w = min(round(1080 * iw / ih), 1920), h = min(round(1920 * ih / iw), 1080), round = half up on integers (a*b + c/2) / c
geometry.offset: x = floor((1920 - w) / 2), y = floor((1080 - h) / 2); odd offsets are kept (pad runs on RGBA)
geometry.correction: the previous scale.rs rounded offsets down to even; wrong for odd-difference sizes (720x576, 1920x1088, 412x236, ...)

paths.direct: 8-bit picture whose fitted size equals its size (no resampling): the unscaled converter below
paths.separable: everything else: any resampling, and every picture above 8 bits including same-size 10-bit

direct_path.arithmetic: per pixel l = (Y - off) * cy + 2^14; per 2x2 block (nearest chroma) r = floor(V' * crv / 2^14) * 2^14, g = floor(-U' * cgu / 2^14) * 2^14 + floor(-V' * cgv / 2^14) * 2^14, b = floor(U' * cbu / 2^14) * 2^14 with U' = U - 128, V' = V - 128; out = clamp((l + term) >> 15, 0, 255). Implemented in 16-bit lanes as ((l >> 14) + term / 2^14) >> 1, identical because every chroma term is a multiple of 2^14.
direct_path.constants: cy = 38156, off = 16 (limited) or cy = 32768, off = 0 (full); [crv, cbu, cgu, cgv] per matrix in harness/codecs/rgba-coefficients-dev-mac.json (each exact on every pixel of a random 1920x1080 frame)
direct_path.matrices: 1 -> BT.709, 4 -> FCC, 7 -> SMPTE 240M, 9 -> BT.2020 NCL, everything else BT.601

separable_path.planes: luma W x H -> w x h; each chroma plane ceil(W/2) x ceil(H/2) -> ceil(w/2) x h, resampled exactly like luma (same position rule, no chroma siting offset). Observed: blue channel with constant luma and per-column / per-row chroma patterns (1280x720: 640 -> 960 and 360 -> 1080) is exact only with the luma centre rule (offset scan +-40000 / 65536 units; peak at 0, 100% exact).
separable_path.horizontal_pass: per output S = sum(tap14 * sample) with 14-bit taps summing to 16384; intermediate = min(S >> (bit_depth - 1), 32767); no lower clamp (negative intermediates kept: removing the lower clamp took grey upscales from 98.1% to 100% exact)
separable_path.vertical_pass: per output row A = sum(tap12 * intermediate) with 12-bit taps summing to 4096; value = (A + 2^18) >> 19. Luma value is NOT clamped (may be < 0 or > 255, e.g. 10-bit 1022 -> 256); chroma value is clamped to 0..255 before the tables
separable_path.chroma_use: each chroma output sample serves output pixels 2i and 2i+1 (observed: equal blue for every pair with constant luma)
separable_path.same_size_dimension: a dimension whose size is unchanged uses one tap of 16384 (resp. 4096): a copy at the pass precision
separable_path.ten_bit: same path with shift 9 (bits - 1); constant fields show every output transition 4 codes apart ((v + 2) >> 2 to 8 bits); no dither observed: constant fields stay uniform and random 1920x1080, 3840x2160, 416x240, 1280x720 10-bit frames are exact with the model

conversion.form: R = G(y + rv(v)), Gc = G(y + gu(u) + gv(v)), B = G(y + bu(u)) with y the unclamped luma value, u, v the clamped chroma values, integer offsets in luma steps and G the grey ramp clamped at its ends; A = 255
conversion.offsets: off(c) = floor(c * inc / 2^16) - floor(128 * inc / 2^16) for c in 0..255
conversion.inc_note: each value is the middle of the fitted range in harness/codecs/rgba-tables-dev-mac.json; every value in a range yields the identical 256-entry table, so the choice is exact
conversion.observations: Per matrix and range, 256 chroma values x 64 luma levels for each of V (U = 128) and U (V = 128) on 16x16 constant blocks through a 512 -> 520 rescale, each offset the unique integer explaining all 64 outputs; 4096 random (Y, U, V) triples predicted 100% exactly by the additive form
conversion.refused: matrices 8 (YCgCo), 10 (BT.2020 CL), 11+ make the reference graph fail to configure; the Scaler falls back to BT.601 for them

taps.position: inc = round(n * 2^16 / m) (integer division with +m/2); output x is centred at c = (x * inc + (inc - 2^16) / 2) / 2^16 source samples. Observed: per-output centre fits on 1280 -> 1920 give inc 8738.0 / 43691 exactly; the half unit is real (offset scan: 0 mismatching rows at +0.5, 88-146 at the integer neighbours)
taps.kernel: Keys cubic, a = -0.6 (Mitchell-Netravali B = 0, C = 0.6), at |k - c| / s with s = max(n / m, 1), the exact ratio (s = inc / 2^16 fails 98 of 1728 rows on 2560 -> 1728)
taps.window: 4 taps when upscaling, ceil(4 n / m) when downscaling (odd sizes too: 264 -> 240 uses 5), starting at floor(c - (size - 1) / 2 + 1/2); when that start is negative it is ceil(c - (size - 1) / 2) instead (left edge only; drops an out-of-range tap instead of folding it, observed on 176 -> 1320, 416 -> 1872, 20 -> 1000, 264 -> 240, 2560 -> 1728 ...)
taps.trim: outputs visited from last to first: drop a window's first tap while the running sum of dropped |K| (raw kernel units, K summing to about s) stays <= 1/3000 (= 0.002 / 6) and the start stays below the next output's start. Brackets: upscale [3.31e-4, 3.34e-4] relative; 1056 -> 135 0.0016-0.0020 after x 6s; trailing near-zero taps are kept (120 -> 1080 row 418)
taps.fold: taps outside the source add onto the edge sample (right edge always; left edge after the window rule)
taps.kernel_rounding: horizontal (14-bit) passes round each kernel value to a multiple of 2^-30 before normalising; vertical (12-bit) passes use it exactly. Found from near-ties: on 88 -> 660 six rows whose exact running value lies 5.8e-9 .. 7.7e-6 tap units from a rounding tie are all predicted only by 2^-30 rounding (searched 2^-26 .. 2^-39, round/trunc/floor); applying the same to vertical passes breaks 110 -> 1920 / 154 -> 1920. Round-half-up, truncation, floor and half-away at 2^-29..2^-31 were compared on all horizontal data: round at 2^-30 leaves 3 rows, every other variant 3-9.
taps.quantisation: normalise to 16384 (horizontal) or 4096 (vertical), then left to right v = w * one / sum + carry, tap = floor(v + 1/2), carry = v - tap (error diffusion); exact rational arithmetic (i128 in Rust)
taps.measurement: Single-sample impulses (+127 / -128 on 128) through the reference scale filter with gray16le output (1 code = 1/64 tap unit; the 19-bit path S >> 3, then (h + 4) >> 3 explains every observation with a unique integer tap), rows as independent horizontal experiments and columns as vertical ones
taps.measured_mismatches: 4 of 65746 rows, all near-ties the model resolves the other way: h 1056->135 x=121 (exact value 1.7e-5 tap units from the tie), h 1920->1906 x=1268 (2.4e-5), h 960->1906 x=1668 (2.8e-5), h 206->1885 x=1840 (5.2e-5). They need a kernel error of ~1.5e-9..3e-9 relative, more than 2^-30 rounding gives, while 88->660 bounds it to ~2.4e-10..5.2e-10 on other rows; fixed-point Horner/power evaluations in Q30 fit worse (6-10 rows). Open.

odd_width_stage.chroma: each chroma plane is resampled to the full fitted width (cw -> fw, same tap rule) and the fitted height
odd_width_stage.arithmetic: v = (A + 2^9) >> 10 for each plane (A = unrounded vertical sum); y' = v_y - 16 * 2^9 (limited) or v_y (full), u' = v_u - 128 * 2^9, v' = v_v - 128 * 2^9; R = clamp(wrap32(y' * cy + v' * crv + 2^21) >> 22), G = ... - u' * cgu - v' * cgv, B = ... + u' * cbu, alpha 255. The sum wraps as a 32-bit integer, so results of 512 levels and above come out black (observed).
odd_width_stage.observations: Random 64x48 -> 101x76 pictures; full-range luma-only thresholds pin v = (A + 512) >> 10 and out = (v + 256) >> 9 exactly (offset bracket [513/1024, 513/1024 + 4e-6]); limited luma gives the unique cy = 9539 at 22 fractional bits; per matrix/range a search of the five coefficients around a quarter of the direct-path constants finds exactly one solution reproducing every channel of every pixel (incl. the wrapped ones)

real_pictures.method: harness/codecs/validate_rgba.py, MAX_FRAMES=30: FFmpeg-decoded planes of every h264/hevc vector in harness/codecs/correctness-manifest.json plus the six .research/codec-inputs video workloads, converted by the probe (== reference_decode chain) and by the release Scaler; converter-only comparison

evidence_scripts.harness/codecs/probe_rgba.c: reference chain on crafted planes (PROBE_CHAIN override, PROBE_BENCH timing)
evidence_scripts.harness/codecs/rgba_full_model.py: numpy twin of the whole path vs the probe
evidence_scripts.harness/codecs/validate_rgba.py: real decoded pictures (FFmpeg-decoded planes) through both converters

performance_dev_mac.harness: Median of 200 conversions of one picture, reference = probe_rgba PROBE_BENCH (buffersrc add + buffersink get, graph nb_threads 1), ours = release Scaler::letterbox (raw_letterbox hook, --test-threads=1); identical bytes checked; run twice, no competing benchmark of ours (other agents' jobs were present on the machine: load ~3)
performance_dev_mac.notes: the reference's same-size 8-bit converter is a NEON kernel (0.33 ms per 1080p picture on the M3 Pro); ours is an auto-vectorised 16-bit-lane row kernel. The first ~30 conversions after start run 2-3x slower on this Mac (frequency/core ramp), so short runs mislead. Mac numbers do not establish Linux or TV performance.

reference_crop.finding: with libavcodec's default apply_cropping the reference decoder applies a left crop only as far as its plane pointers stay aligned (public AVCodecContext.apply_cropping documentation); the frames its filter graph letterboxes therefore keep part or all of the left crop border. Top, right and bottom crops are applied in full.
reference_crop.rule: per-plane byte offsets of the cropped origin o_luma = top * pitch + left * bps, o_chroma = (top/2) * (pitch/2) + (left/2) * bps; m = min ctz(o); if m < 5 the kept left crop is left & ~((1 << (5 + ctz(left) - m)) - 1), else left
reference_crop.pitch: reference row pitch = coded width in bytes rounded up to 32 (observed 176->192, 352, 416, 528->544, 1056, 1920 8-bit; 3840 bytes for 1920 10-bit); chroma pitch = half
reference_crop.observations: h264_metadata / hevc_metadata re-cropped streams: 8-bit crop_left 2..48 -> 0, 64 and 96 -> 64, 128 and 160 -> 128; with crop_top 2 or 6 (chroma origin 16-byte aligned) crop_left 64 -> 0, with top 4 or 8 -> 64; 10-bit crop_left 16 -> 0, 32/34/48 -> 32, 64 -> 64, 96 -> 96. Conformance vectors: CVFC1_Sony_C (352x288, crop 26/26/60/60) delivered 326x168; CONFWIN_A_Sony_1 (416x240, crop 2 each side) delivered 414x236
reference_crop.implementation: scale::reference_crop derives (top, left) from the luma plane layout (offset = top * stride + left over the whole decoded plane, codec::Plane docs) and widens the view by the re-included columns; pitch taken as stride rounded up to 32 bytes (exact for the h264 decoder's stride = coded width and for 8-bit hevc stride = align(width, 32); for 10-bit hevc with both top and left crop the chroma pitch parity can differ from the reference's)
reference_crop.contract_dependency: needs the decoders to hand over whole planes with the crop offset. The hevc adapter does (Plane::raw); the h264 adapter passes data starting at the visible origin (codec-h264 Plane::data), so on the native codec-worker path CVFC1_Sony_C stays wrong until codec-h264 exposes the whole plane and crates/sim/src/adapters.rs passes it with offset = crop_y * stride + crop_x (as for hevc)
reference_crop.verification: reference_decode raw output vs the Scaler on whole coded planes with the crop offsets: CVFC1_Sony_C 50/50 pictures exact, CONFWIN_A_Sony_1 60/60 exact; these are the only two h264/hevc manifest vectors with a left or top crop
